articles.title: Mark Zuckerberg and his wife make an extravagant wish come true with billionaire money
articles.standfirst: Their latest purchase looks straight out of a fairy tale
articles.summary: Their latest purchase looks straight out of a fairy tale
articles.body:
T here comes a point when billionaire money can turn an almost childlike fantasy into something very real. For Mark Zuckerberg and his wife, Priscilla Chan , that now apparently means being able to say they have a castle of their own.

The Meta CEO and Chan have purchased Strancally Castle, a striking 19th-century Gothic Revival property in County Waterford, Ireland, according to multiple reports. A spokesperson for Zuckerberg has confirmed the acquisition, saying the family is excited to care for the historic home and spend time in Ireland. The price remains private, but the estate has been valued at between €20 million and €30 million roughly $23 million to $35 million.

And this is no mansion simply borrowing the word “castle.” Built around 1830, Strancally rises above the River Blackwater and sits within roughly 440 acres of countryside.

The three-story property has undergone extensive restoration over the past two decades, turning an aging piece of Irish history into the kind of secluded retreat that very few people in the world could ever call home.

Zuckerberg and Chan bought the estate from Michael and Giancarla Alen-Buckley, whose family had owned it for about 25 years . The former owners said they were leaving with fond memories after having the opportunity to save and restore the property, while expressing satisfaction that its new owners intend to continue investing in the house and grounds. The deal was completed privately and off-market several weeks ago.

The castle will not replace the couple's life in the United States. Instead, it is expected to become their home when spending time in Ireland, a country with a particularly important connection to Zuckerberg's business empire: Meta has its international headquarters in Dublin and employs around 1,500 people in the country.

Perhaps the most extraordinary part is that buying a castle is only the latest chapter in the couple's remarkable real-estate story. Zuckerberg and Chan have amassed extensive property in Hawaii, and earlier this year they were reported to have paid $170 million for a waterfront mansion on Miami's ultra-exclusive Indian Creek Island.

For most people, owning a castle belongs to childhood stories, movies or a dream that disappears somewhere along the way to adulthood. For Zuckerberg and Chan, extraordinary wealth has made that fantasy a set of keys.

Their new retreat comes with hundreds of acres, a river at its doorstep, and nearly two centuries of history, proving that when money is no longer an obstacle, even the most extravagant wishes can become reality.

articles.title: A man steps into the ring and faces a humanoid robot in a scene from another world
articles.body:
T here is no doubt that 2026 is showing just how quickly artificial intelligence and robotics are advancing . Humanoid robots have moved beyond demonstrations limited to standing, walking or performing simple movements. Now, they are starring in increasingly striking scenes.

One of them took place during the 2026 World Robot Conference in Beijing , where different companies showcased their latest developments and demonstrated just how far these machines can go.

What happened during the demonstration?

A man stepped into the ring and faced a humanoid robot in a sparring session in front of conference attendees , creating a scene that looked like something out of an intense dream.

Inside the ring, the two exchanged punches while the robot responded to the movements of the person standing in front of it.

But is this really something new?

Not exactly. Robots fighting is not a completely new sight . In 2025, several demonstrations began gaining attention as machines faced each other inside a ring.

Humanoid robots had also been seen performing martial arts moves, acrobatics and exercises designed to showcase their balance and coordination.

However, the images from Beijing introduce an important change: this time, the opponent was not another robot, but a person.

How often is the World Robot Conference held?

The World Robot Conference takes place every year in August, bringing together new developments and existing technologies from the world of robotics. People from different countries can also attend and participate in the event .

articles.title: Galaxy S26: 3 camera features you need to know to get the most out of your phone
articles.standfirst: The phone has more than one hidden surprise.
articles.summary: The phone has more than one hidden surprise.
articles.body:
The Galaxy S26 continues to get attention from users and, beyond the features that usually get the most attention , its camera hides several tools that can change the way you use the phone. Finding them simply requires exploring a few settings and options that aren't always easy to spot.

Among them are four features worth knowing. Each serves a different purpose, from getting better results when taking photos to having more control when recording videos , plus an option that can be especially useful in everyday situations.

24 MP: an option right in the middle

Let's start with one of the features that can be easiest to overlook: 24 MP mode.

The Galaxy S26 offers 12 MP and 50 MP options, but there's also this middle-ground alternative that aims to combine the best of both . Through AI Fusion processing, the phone uses higher-resolution information and computational photography techniques to produce images with more detail than 12 MP shots, without reaching the file size of a 50 MP photo.

The catch? It isn't immediately visible.

To use it, you need to download Good Lock from the Galaxy Store and install the Camera Assistant module. Then, go into the camera settings, turn on the 24 MP option and return to Photo mode .

The 24M option will then appear.

It's an interesting alternative if you want a little more detail in your photos without having every image take up as much storage space as a 50 MP shot.

Virtual Reflector lets you play with light

The second feature takes a completely different approach.

Virtual Reflector has nothing to do with photo resolution. Instead, it focuses on something that can make a huge difference in the final result: lighting .

The tool allows you to virtually adjust the color, intensity and direction of the light reflected onto the subject. The idea is based on something photographers often do with physical reflectors, but here the adjustment is handled directly through software .

To find it, open Expert RAW, Samsung's app for users who want greater control over their photos. The Virtual Reflector option can be found in the Labs section, where you can experiment with the lighting.

And this is where the Galaxy S26's camera starts offering something different: instead of simply taking a photo and accepting the way the light looks, you have more options for adjusting it .

Horizontal Lock keeps your videos from looking tilted

Now let's move on to video.

The Galaxy S26 also features Horizontal Lock, a tool found within Super Steady that aims to keep the horizon level while recording.

The feature uses the phone's motion sensors to detect how you're moving and keep the frame as level as possible. That means the horizon can remain steady even if you tilt or rotate the phone while recording.

To activate it, open Video, select Super Steady and look for the horizontal lock icon.

There is one detail to keep in mind: Horizontal Lock requires good lighting conditions to work. If the environment is too dark, the feature may not be available .

For anyone who records while walking, follows moving subjects or simply wants steadier videos without using additional accessories, it can be a very practical tool.

articles.title: Elon Musk warns about the change mobile phones will undergo before 2030
articles.standfirst: Artificial intelligence will be key in this project
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence will be key in this project
articles.body:
Elon Musk, among his multiple projects, would have the manufacture of a mobile phone powered by artificial intelligence (AI) , a rumor that began last year, 2025, but which is still not underway, as he himself explained on the podcast "Joe Rogan Experience".'

For the moment, he assured that manufacturing will not begin "unless necessary", since he does not want to launch a mobile phone onto the market, but rather "a way that is very different from the most traditional sense of what a mobile phone is".

'“We will not have a mobile phone in the traditional sense. What we will call a phone will actually be a peripheral node for AI inference with wireless connections. The artificial intelligence on the server will communicate with the AI on your device and generate real-time video of anything you can imagine" , was his explanation.'

Elon Musk's estimate for being able to begin its development

And this device would not be subject to operating systems or applications; it will only have a screen and audio, with AI and the human as the central focus: "Anything you can think of, or really anything AI can anticipate you might want, it will show you. Probably within five or six years."

He already presented this idea at a Neuralink event, in 2025 : “In the future, physical devices such as smartphones will be obsolete,” he stated, since everything will go through implants and AI: “In a few years, these implants will be safe and advanced enough to be adopted on a massive scale”.

He wants to create people directly connected with technology, something that began in January 2024, when Neuralink achieved a technological milestone by implanting its first brain chip in Noland Arbaugh, who had quadriplegia after an accident in 2016.

Thanks to this device, Arbaugh regained digital autonomy by controlling a computer with his mind, even being able to play video games.

articles.title: ChatGPT goes silent as 74,000 outage reports pour in and OpenAI works on a fix
articles.standfirst: Complaints exploded within 30 minutes as elevated errors affected both ChatGPT and Codex
articles.summary: Complaints exploded within 30 minutes as elevated errors affected both ChatGPT and Codex
articles.body:
For a platform designed to answer almost any question, the most frustrating one Thursday morning was also the simplest: Is ChatGPT down? For tens of thousands of users, the chatbot could not even respond.

Reports began climbing at extraordinary speed. More than 5,000 problems had been reported to Downdetector by 7:53 a.m. PT. Ten minutes later, that number had surpassed 22,000. By 8:23 a.m., more than 74,000 reports had poured in.

OpenAI’s status page initially showed no known problems, even as complaints spread online and searches for “Is ChatGPT down?” began trending. At 7:58 a.m. PT, the company officially acknowledged “elevated errors” affecting both ChatGPT and Codex, its AI coding service.

OpenAI applies mitigation as users wait for recovery

At 8:22 a.m. PT, OpenAI announced that it had applied a mitigation and was monitoring the recovery . The incident page listed 15 affected ChatGPT components and four Codex components, although the disruption did not appear to be a complete shutdown for every user.

That helps explain why some people could still access ChatGPT while others encountered failed prompts, slow responses or a service that would not load at all. Large online platforms can suffer partial or intermittent failures that affect particular regions, accounts or features without taking the entire system offline.

The gap between the first user complaints and OpenAI’s acknowledgment is also not necessarily unusual. Downdetector reacts immediately to sudden increases in public reports, while a company must first detect, verify and classify an incident before changing its official status page. Its figures represent submitted reports, not a confirmed count of every person affected.

OpenAI has not yet explained what went wrong or confirmed that the problem is completely over . But the reaction said plenty: ChatGPT has become part of how people work, study and get through their day and when it suddenly goes silent, they feel its absence immediately.
